declared_purpose: Manage user-selected Baidu Netdisk files within /apps/bdpan/, with supporting authentication and lifecycle management; back up, list and restore memory for kimiclaw/maxclaw/qclaw/openclaw. The declared memory scope is seven named workspace files, memory/*.md and manifest.json. These are explicit requirements; hostname-based device identifiers, staging methods and snapshot timing are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md:4-8, 15-15, 249-280, 307-317.

data_operations.operation: Check authentication and return account metadata
data_operations.source: Entry prerequisites and login/memory wrappers invoking bdpan whoami
data_operations.data_scope: Authentication status; documented username and token expiry. The memory wrapper reduces the result to loggedIn.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI and its caller; displayed login results go to standard output. Further CLI network activity is unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Each triggered operation is instructed to check login; login.sh also checks before and after authorization.

data_operations.operation: List and search remote file metadata
data_operations.source: Documented bdpan ls/search commands and existence/size checks
data_operations.data_scope: Requested paths, search keywords and filters; returned filenames, paths, sizes, types and timestamps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Baidu Netdisk through the external CLI; results return to the caller and may be displayed to the user.
data_operations.condition: Explicit listing/search, upload collision checks, download existence/size checks, or share existence checks.

data_operations.operation: Read and upload selected local files
data_operations.data_scope: User-selected file or directory contents and destination names.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: User's Baidu Netdisk account under /apps/bdpan/.
data_operations.condition: Upload request; local existence and remote collision checks are instructed. Entry confirmation rules are inconsistent.

data_operations.operation: Download files or transfer shared files
data_operations.data_scope: Selected remote contents, share links and extraction codes; local and remote destination paths.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Direct downloads write the local destination. Transfer writes the user's Baidu Netdisk account. Shared-link download first stages files in /apps/bdpan/{date}/ or the specified transfer directory, then writes locally.
data_operations.condition: Requested download or transfer. Existing local targets can be overwritten after the instructed confirmation. Remote staging cleanup is undocumented.

data_operations.operation: Persist download output and poll progress
data_operations.data_scope: bdpan download standard output/error, process status and local destination file metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/bdpan-dl-<shell PID>.log; polling output returns to the caller and progress is reported to the user.
data_operations.condition: Files larger than 50 MB. Cleanup is instructed using a PID-based filename that may differ from the created filename.

data_operations.operation: Create externally accessible file shares
data_operations.data_scope: Selected files or entire selected folders; generated link, extraction code and expiry.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Baidu Netdisk sharing service; anyone possessing the link and extraction code can access shared contents. Credentials are returned to the caller/user.
data_operations.condition: Requested sharing. Default expiry is seven days; permanent sharing follows an expressed long-term preference. Public-sharing confirmation is explicitly required in the examples.

data_operations.operation: Mutate or delete remote files
data_operations.data_scope: Selected remote paths, names and file contents; copying creates another remote copy.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: User's Baidu Netdisk account within /apps/bdpan/.
data_operations.condition: Requested operation. Deletion requires confirmation; its CLI implementation and server-side deletion semantics are absent.

data_operations.operation: Collect and delegate an authorization code
data_operations.data_scope: CLI-generated AUTH_URL and user-entered AUTH_CODE. Invalid input is printed; valid input is passed through stdin and subsequently unset.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Authorization URL goes to terminal/caller and the user's browser. AUTH_CODE goes to the bdpan child process; its exchange with Baidu is implemented externally.
data_operations.condition: Not already logged in; confirmation precedes obtaining the URL unless the script's automation option is used. The entry prohibits agents from using that option.

data_operations.operation: Document credential persistence and refresh
data_operations.source: Authentication reference describing external bdpan behavior
data_operations.data_scope: OAuth tokens; password storage is disclaimed in the documentation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Documented local configuration at ~/.config/bdpan/config.json, subject to CLI configuration overrides.
data_operations.condition: Successful login and subsequent token use. Encryption and automatic refresh are documentation claims, not inspectable implementations.

data_operations.operation: Infer agent environment and derive device identity
data_operations.source: Memory script detection and manifest generation
data_operations.data_scope: Script location, directory existence, HOME, OPENCLAW_HOME and OPENCLAW_CLI determine agent/workspace. Hostname becomes a normalized device identifier. Manifest adds agent, constant memory-system name, timestamps, backup type and filenames.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Detection inputs are local. Derived agent/device identifiers enter Baidu Netdisk paths; manifest metadata is staged locally and uploaded.
data_operations.condition: Memory backup/list/restore in a supported environment. Backup creates the manifest.

data_operations.operation: Stage and upload memory backups
data_operations.data_scope: Existing seven named workspace files, immediate memory/*.md files and manifest.json. Copies follow selected source-file symlinks.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary memory-backup directory, then user's Baidu Netdisk at /apps/bdpan/agent-memory/<agent>/<device>/manual/<timestamp>/.
data_operations.condition: backup invocation in a supported environment after prerequisites. The script has no upload confirmation prompt; each backup uses a timestamped path.

data_operations.operation: List backups and retrieve a restore manifest
data_operations.source: Memory script list/restore and manifest readers
data_operations.data_scope: Current agent/device backup directory names; selected manifest's agent, device, memory system, timestamps and file paths.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Baidu Netdisk listing requests; metadata returns to local parsers/caller. Restore manifest is downloaded to a temporary directory.
data_operations.condition: list or restore invocation. Restore requires one matching backup; compatibility mismatches stop restoration unless forced. Manifest paths reject absolute paths and parent traversal.

data_operations.operation: Persist a local pre-restore safety snapshot
data_operations.data_scope: Entire current memory directory recursively, plus existing seven workspace files.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: <workspace>/.backup-before-restore/<timestamp>/; no pruning or deletion of this snapshot is implemented.
data_operations.condition: After manifest retrieval/compatibility handling, before file downloads and overwrite confirmation. The snapshot therefore also occurs on subsequent cancellation or noninteractive refusal.

data_operations.operation: Download manifest-selected files and merge into local workspace
data_operations.data_scope: Every accepted manifest file entry, including relative paths beyond the declared memory set. Existing targets are overwritten; other local files are retained.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary memory-restore directory, then WORKSPACE_DIR or MEMORY_DIR.
data_operations.condition: Payload downloads precede confirmation. Merge requires interactive approval or --yes; only successfully downloaded files are copied.

data_operations.operation: Delete temporary memory staging directories
data_operations.data_scope: Locally staged backup contents, restore manifest and downloaded restore payloads.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: _BACKUP_TMP_DIR and _RESTORE_TMP_DIR; persistent safety snapshots and cloud backups are outside this cleanup.
data_operations.condition: Shell EXIT trap execution, including ordinary failure or cancellation.

data_operations.operation: Download and execute an external installer
data_operations.data_scope: Locally detected OS/architecture select a versioned installer URL, revealing that platform selection to the download recipient. Installer bytes are saved locally and executed; registration is delegated to bdpan install --force.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Initial download host issuecdn.baidupcs.com; installer in the current directory, then external installer/CLI processes. Installer is deleted after successful execution.
data_operations.condition: Install invocation, or missing CLI during memory prerequisites. --skip-download uses the user-specified local BDPAN_BIN instead. Execution confirmation can be bypassed by installer flags; external installer behavior is unknown.

data_operations.operation: Check for updates and replace skill files
data_operations.data_scope: Local VERSION is read and compared locally. Remote configuration and update archive are retrieved. Presence of CLAUDE_CODE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and MCP_SERVER controls confirmation; their values are not added to the scripted requests.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configuration request to https://pan.baidu.com/act/v2/api/conf?conf_key=bd_skills; archive request to the configured, initially allowlisted host. Archive is temporary; extraction and VERSION persist in SKILL_DIR.
data_operations.condition: Explicitly requested update/check. --check still contacts the configuration service. Archive download requires an update decision; checksum verification precedes extraction. Temporary archive directory has EXIT cleanup.

data_operations.operation: Publish the package through ClawHub
data_operations.data_scope: ClawHub account identity, local Git dirty-state check, package directory, version, display name and optional changelog.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Identity and command details go to caller/terminal. Package publishing is delegated to ClawHub; exact uploaded file selection and service endpoint are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Separate publish-script invocation with installed/authenticated clawhub and a valid version; confirmation unless --yes. This path is not called by normal Netdisk operations.

data_operations.operation: Inspect installation metadata and delete local credentials/configuration
data_operations.source: Logout documentation, troubleshooting reset and scripts/uninstall.sh
data_operations.data_scope: Binary version/path, configuration file count and login state; deletion of the selected configuration directory and CLI binary.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Metadata stays with caller/terminal. Default deletion boundaries are ~/.config/bdpan/ and ~/.local/bin/bdpan, with environment/path overrides. Logout behavior is delegated to bdpan.
data_operations.condition: Requested logout, troubleshooting reset, or uninstall; uninstall confirms unless --yes. No packaged implementation establishes remote session revocation.

data_operations.operation: Create, upload and remove an archive in an optional backup example
data_operations.data_scope: Contents of ~/important-data/ recursively, archived with a date-based filename.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local /tmp archive, then user's Baidu Netdisk backup directory; sample subsequently removes the local archive.
data_operations.condition: Only if the example is adopted and executed; no packaged scheduler or automatic invocation is shown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Invalid AUTH_CODE input, potentially including a mistyped credential or another accidentally pasted secret.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: scripts/login.sh standard output and its terminal/tool caller.
potential_excess.condition: Authorization input fails the format check.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Login needs validation and submission of a valid authorization code; repeating rejected input is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reject invalid input and explain the expected format.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the output containing AUTH_CODE; report only the validation failure.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep format validation, stdin submission of valid codes and credential cleanup. This removes extra data from an otherwise necessary error response.

potential_excess.data_scope: Hostname-derived device identity, which can retain personal or organizational naming information after normalization.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: User's Baidu Netdisk backup path and uploaded manifest.json; also displayed backup/list paths.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared storage layout requires device separation; it does not require disclosure of the machine's actual hostname.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Consistently identify the same device for backup discovery and restoration.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a stable, locally stored opaque device identifier instead of the hostname.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Use the same identifier in paths and manifests; retain a mapping or migration path for existing hostname-based backups.

potential_excess.data_scope: Contents outside the intended memory roots reached through a selected workspace or memory-file symlink.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Temporary memory-backup directory, then user's Baidu Netdisk timestamped backup.
potential_excess.condition: A selected filename is a symlink to an external regular file; the file test accepts it and cp follows its referent.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared purpose selects agent memory files, while this implementation does not check the resolved source boundary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Back up the declared memory contents.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Validate resolved source paths against approved memory/workspace boundaries before copying; exclude external referents unless explicitly included in the requested scope.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue backing up ordinary selected files and supported in-scope links. This narrows uploaded contents, rather than removing the required backup action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Nested, hidden or non-Markdown files inside the current memory directory.
potential_excess.condition: Restore reaches the safety-net block and the memory directory exists.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry declares memory/*.md plus seven workspace files as backup contents. The safety implementation recursively copies the entire memory directory.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve current declared memory before overwriting it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Apply the declared memory-file selection to safety snapshots instead of recursively copying every directory entry.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain all declared memory needed for rollback; include additional file types only where an expanded memory scope is established. The safety action remains necessary; its copied data can be narrowed.

potential_excess.data_scope: A duplicate of current local memory despite no approved restore taking place.
potential_excess.condition: The script creates a safety snapshot, then the user cancels or noninteractive execution is refused.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The safety snapshot protects against restore overwrites; those branches perform no merge.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preview affected files, obtain approval and preserve rollback data before the first overwrite.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Create the safety snapshot after approval and immediately before apply_merge.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Abort before modifying targets if the required safety copy fails. This avoids a redundant snapshot on cancellation, rather than removing the snapshot from an approved restore.

potential_excess.data_scope: Manifest-listed files outside the seven workspace filenames and immediate memory/*.md scope.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Temporary restore directory and subsequently arbitrary accepted relative locations within the workspace.
potential_excess.condition: A nonstandard or modified remote manifest includes additional relative paths. Normal script-generated manifests use the declared selection.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Memory restoration has an explicit file scope, but validation only rejects absolute paths and parent traversal; apply_merge accepts other relative filenames.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve and restore the declared memory files from the selected backup.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Enforce the declared file allowlist when reading the manifest, before downloading payloads or merging them.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Accept all normal generated manifests and supported compatibility metadata; require an established expanded scope for other payloads. This removes extra files from the required restore action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Background download standard output/error; exact contents depend on the external CLI.
potential_excess.condition: The recipe substitutes the returned background-process PID into polling/cleanup commands. Creation uses $$, while the returned PID is $!, so cleanup can target a different filename.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Logging supports progress and error reporting; retaining an orphaned log after completion is unnecessary for the requested download.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide reliable background progress and diagnose failures.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Track and return the actual log pathname together with the process PID, and delete that same file when reporting is complete.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the log available while polling or reporting an error. This narrows persistence without removing required progress reporting.

unknowns: All supplied packaged source was reviewed. The bdpan executable is absent, so actual API endpoints, authorization scopes, implicit update requests, telemetry and internal file handling remain unresolved.

Token encryption, automatic refresh and local credential deletion are documented claims; implementation and remote revocation cannot be verified (reference/authentication.md:41-47, 100-104; scripts/uninstall.sh:126-138).

Shared-link download requires documented cloud staging, but subsequent retention or cleanup is unspecified. A redundant permanent cloud copy cannot be established from this source (reference/bdpan-commands.md:127-130).

The external installer, registration command and downloaded update archive are not supplied. Their additional reads, disclosures and writes cannot be audited (scripts/install.sh:251-265; scripts/update.sh:217-230).
Download requests permit redirects. Final redirected recipients are not established by the initial CDN URL or updater host allowlist (scripts/install.sh:184-187; scripts/update.sh:126-156, 180-186).
ClawHub's selected upload files, credential handling, publication visibility and retention are external and unresolved; publishing is a separate maintainer path (scripts/publish.sh:91-97, 155-164).
CLI output contents and downstream retention by terminals or agent callers are unknown. A normal tool return alone does not establish further remote disclosure.

Confirmation guidance conflicts: writes/public shares require explicit confirmation, while the risk table allows several such operations directly. Memory backup has no internal upload prompt (SKILL.md:28-37, 82-86; scripts/memory-backup.sh:466-541).

Runtime file contents, symlinks and remote manifests are not supplied; the conditional excess scopes cannot be measured. Cloud backup and local safety-snapshot retention periods are unspecified, so retaining history alone is not established as excess.
